reason: The text introduces multiple named characters who are clearly regular people: Elkanah (איש אחד - 'a man'), explicitly identified as from Ramathaim Zophim in the hill country of Ephraim; his two wives Hannah (חנה) and Peninnah (פננה); Eli the priest (עלי); and his sons Hophni (חפני) and Pinchas (פנחס). While some have religious roles, they are portrayed as ordinary humans dealing with realistic concerns such as infertility, family relationships, and religious observance. The narrative focuses on their personal struggles and daily life rather than extraordinary or supernatural qualities.
